chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Hammad ibn 'Isa, from Rib'i, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abi Ja'far عليه السلام, who said:

I said to him: May a man perform salat (prayer) while veiling his mouth with a cloth? He said: "As for on the ground, no; but as for on a riding animal, there is no harm." And if his garment is over his mouth? He said: "There is no harm in that, if he can hear the murmuring."
Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, said: It is disliked for a woman to perform salat (prayer) while wearing a niqab when she has the ability and the choice.

key_terms.الِاخْتِيَارِ: having choice and not being under compulsion
key_terms.الْهَمْهَمَةَ: a low audible murmur of recitation
key_terms.فِيهِ: his mouth, referring to the place covered by the garment
key_terms.مُتَلَثِّمٌ: covering the mouth or lower face with a cloth
key_terms.نِقَابٌ: a face veil worn by a woman

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to perform salat (prayer) while covering the mouth or wearing a niqab?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses rulings related to covering the mouth during salat (prayer). It indicates that praying while veiled over the mouth is not allowed on the ground, while it is permitted on a riding animal, and covering the mouth with a garment is not problematic if the recitation remains audible as a murmur. Al-Shaykh adds that it is disliked for a woman to pray in a niqab when not compelled.
